name: Meeri
summary: Shopify app that recovers abandoned carts with AI-written web push notifications instead of email or SMS. No address or phone is needed to subscribe, and there is no commission on recovered revenue.
best_for: small Shopify stores that want a cart-recovery channel which costs almost nothing and takes no commission on what it recovers, and that are willing to treat the free 300 notifications a month as a measurement of their own push opt-in rate before paying anything
skip_if: you need the recovered contacts anywhere other than the browser that opted in, you run recovery through Klaviyo, Postscript or another stack you want this to feed, or you cannot get the usage-based charge on Pro quoted as a rate before you enable it
honest_knock:
Start with the numbers on the vendor’s own homepage, because they do not match the App Store. Read on 19 September 2026, meeritech.com still says “5.0 on Shopify App Store”, “100% five-star reviews” and “5.0 average — 8 verified reviews on Shopify” — word for word what it said on 23 August. The listing that same morning shows 4.7 from 11 reviews: ten at five stars and one at one star. So the vendor’s figure is what you get by leaving the single bad review out, and its review count has stood still while the real one moved. Nothing about the app is settled by that, but a marketing page that rounds its own rating up by dropping the worst review, and then does not refresh it for a month, is a useful thing to know before you weigh the rest of the page.

The review base is thin whichever number you use. Eleven reviews on an app that launched in February 2024, and the three the listing shows first come from one store in the United Kingdom and two in Pakistan, one of which had been using the app for seven days when it wrote. That is not evidence of anything wrong; it is very little evidence of anything at all, and it cannot tell you how this behaves on a store like yours.

Then there is the channel itself, which is the real decision. Web push needs a browser-level subscription, and the app’s own pitch is that no email or phone number is required to get one. That cuts both ways: the list is easier to build and worthless off the browser that built it. You cannot export those subscribers into an email tool, you cannot reach them anywhere else, and your recovery ceiling is set by opt-in rate rather than by the app. Measure the opt-in rate first, 300 free notifications a month is enough to find out, because it decides everything the paid plan can do for you.

One more limit worth reading before you install: the listing names English as the only language, and Shopify Admin as the only integration. There is no Klaviyo, no email platform, no SMS tool on that line, so this sits beside your existing stack rather than inside it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per month for 3,000 email and push notification messages in one allowance, billed in USD every 30 days with a 7-day free trial
pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/meeripush-push-notifications, listed as “Meeri Abandoned Cart Recovery”, and on meeritech.com; both re-read 2026-09-19 with no amount changed; the listing re-read 2026-11-04, same amounts, but the allowances now count email as well as push) Two plans, and the free one is a real plan rather than a demo. Basic is free to install and, on the listing as read on 4 November 2026, covers 100 emails and 300 push notifications, which the listing itself translates as roughly 100 recovered carts; in September the same card named push notifications only. It carries unlimited subscribers and segmentation, the abandoned-cart recovery campaign, scheduled promotional campaigns, AI-generated campaign content, intelligent delivery timing and basic email support, and it takes no commission on recovered revenue. Pro is $4.99 a month with a 7-day free trial and adds 3,000 email and push notification messages in one shared allowance (in September: 3,000 push notification impressions), unlimited campaigns and automations and premium support. All charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The plan text says Pro “upgrades as you grow” and that additional usage-based charges are billed every 30 days, without printing a rate anywhere on the listing. The vendor’s own site sells the same two tiers at the same prices, calling Basic free forever and Pro’s allowance 3,000 notification impressions a month, and it does not print a usage rate either. The app is English-only, works with Shopify Admin and sits in Shopify’s abandoned-cart category. Developer MEERI TECH L.L.C-FZ, Dubai; the app launched on 23 February 2024 and carried 9 App Store reviews in August 2026 and 11 on 19 September 2026.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Meeri on a Shopify development store only in part: the install, the plan page with Basic at $0 and Pro at $4.99, the Pro and Basic approval screens (both asked for a payment method and neither had the test charge sentence, so nothing was approved), and the Automations page with three push stages for abandoned carts (30 minutes, 6 hours and 12 hours) and a preview of the first message. No real recovery message was sent. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme. Install: the Install button in the dialog Install app was clicked at 16:51:21 in our own tab. The App Store name is Meeri Abandoned Cart Recovery; in the dialog and the admin the app is called Meeri: Push Notifications (by MEERI TECH L.L.C-FZ). The dialog This app needs access to asked for View customer data (sensitive data, device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (store owner) and View store data (customers, orders, Online Store). The admin was in English. After the install the app went straight to the page select-package with Pricing Plans; no payment was needed to open Campaigns and Automations afterwards. Core action, recovering an abandoned cart: this was NOT carried out. A real test needs a shopper who agrees to browser push messages and leaves a cart behind, and the first message comes only 30 minutes later; this was not done, and no recovery message was sent to anyone. What we did see (about 16:52, the preview image shows 4:52 PM and the notes also give 16:55): the Automations page with Welcome (Push on, Email off), Browse Abandonment (Push, off) and the Abandoned Cart stages No. 1 (30 minutes after Cart Abandoned), No. 2 (6 hours after Cart Abandoned) and No. 3 (12 hours after Cart Abandoned), all on the channel Push and on by default, with all statistics at 0. The dashboard said 0 Impressions, 0 Clicks, 0% Avg. CTR and USD 0 Total Revenue. The eye button of No. 1 opened a preview of the message: We have saved your cart for you! with the text that there are items in your cart which are selling out fast. For the cart stages only the channel Push was visible; no e-mail step for carts was seen (only the Welcome Email, which is off). Plans: the page Pricing Plans shows Basic $0 / month with 300 Impressions (Up to 300 impressions; Unlimited subscribers and segmentation; Abandoned cart recovery campaigns; Send and schedule campaigns; AI generated contents for campaigns; Intelligent delivery; basic e-mail help) and Pro $4.99 / month with 3K Impressions (All features in free plan; Up to 3000 impressions; Unlimited campaigns and automations; premium help). The app counts impressions everywhere. Differences with the dossier: the App Store listing of 4 November, which the dossier follows, gives Basic 100 e-mails and 300 push notifications a month and Pro 3,000 e-mail and push messages in one allowance, where the app counts impressions (Basic 300, Pro 3K) and shows no separate e-mail allowance; the Shopify screens show an app spending limit of a maximum of $99,00 USD per 30 days, which the dossier does not mention; the dossier says no usage rate is printed, and we saw no rate either. Checkout: Subscribe on Pro opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription for the plan Pro: This app bills you for a recurring subscription and usage charges, $4,99 USD every 30 days, an app spending limit of a maximum of $99,00 USD per 30 days, a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., a Subtotal of $4,99 plus any applicable taxes (it contains only the subscription fee; usage charges come on top, are variable and appear on the invoices), a Total of $4,99 due 24 Nov, the row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. Subscribe on Basic opened the same kind of screen for the plan Free: This app bills you for usage charges, You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it, the same spending limit of $99,00 USD per 30 days, Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. On neither screen was the sentence You will not be billed for this test charge shown, and both asked for a payment method, so nothing was approved. Cancel on the Pro screen gave the message The shop cannot accept the provided charge. and the screen stayed; we went back through the app address. No per-unit usage rate was shown anywhere. Cancelling: no subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled. The way to stop is to uninstall: Settings, Apps, Meeri, Uninstall opens Uninstall Meeri: Push Notifications? with the text that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; the reason was Testing multiple apps. Not tested: a real push opt-in and a real recovery message, an e-mail channel for carts, the Sign up form, Subscribers, making a campaign, the opt-in rate, any paid plan. No theme change was made or saved. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test (Shopify said You've successfully uninstalled Meeri: Push Notifications); the notes give 16:53 for this, which is earlier than the 16:55 given for the Automations page, so the clock times of the last steps are not reliable. No plan was approved and nothing was billed. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app counts impressions where the listing speaks of e-mails and push notifications, the spending limit of $99 per 30 days is not in the dossier, the Basic plan screen also bills usage and asks for a payment method, neither approval screen had the test charge sentence, the Cancel click on the Pro screen gave the message The shop cannot accept the provided charge., and no usage rate was shown.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Meeri on a Shopify development store only in part: the install, the plan page with Basic at $0 and Pro at $4.99, the Pro and Basic approval screens (both asked for a payment method and neither had the test charge sentence, so nothing was approved), and the Automations page with three push stages for abandoned carts (30 minutes, 6 hours and 12 hours) and a preview of the first message. No real recovery message was sent. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme. Install: the Install button in the dialog Install app was clicked at 16:51:21 in our own tab. The App Store name is Meeri Abandoned Cart Recovery; in the dialog and the admin the app is called Meeri: Push Notifications (by MEERI TECH L.L.C-FZ). The dialog This app needs access to asked for View customer data (sensitive data, device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (store owner) and View store data (customers, orders, Online Store). The admin was in English. After the install the app went straight to the page select-package with Pricing Plans; no payment was needed to open Campaigns and Automations afterwards. Core action, recovering an abandoned cart: this was NOT carried out. A real test needs a shopper who agrees to browser push messages and leaves a cart behind, and the first message comes only 30 minutes later; this was not done, and no recovery message was sent to anyone. What we did see (about 16:52, the preview image shows 4:52 PM and the notes also give 16:55): the Automations page with Welcome (Push on, Email off), Browse Abandonment (Push, off) and the Abandoned Cart stages No. 1 (30 minutes after Cart Abandoned), No. 2 (6 hours after Cart Abandoned) and No. 3 (12 hours after Cart Abandoned), all on the channel Push and on by default, with all statistics at 0. The eye button of No. 1 opened a preview of the message: We have saved your cart for you! with the text that there are items in your cart which are selling out fast. For the cart stages only the channel Push was visible; no e-mail step for carts was seen (only the Welcome Email, which is off). The app counts impressions everywhere. Differences with the dossier: the App Store listing of 4 November, which the dossier follows, gives Basic 100 e-mails and 300 push notifications a month and Pro 3,000 e-mail and push messages in one allowance, where the app counts impressions (Basic 300, Pro 3K) and shows no separate e-mail allowance; the Shopify screens show an app spending limit of a maximum of $99,00 USD per 30 days, which the dossier does not mention; the dossier says no usage rate is printed, and we saw no rate either. Checkout: Subscribe on Pro opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription for the plan Pro: This app bills you for a recurring subscription and usage charges, $4,99 USD every 30 days, an app spending limit of a maximum of $99,00 USD per 30 days, a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., a Subtotal of $4,99 plus any applicable taxes (it contains only the subscription fee; usage charges come on top, are variable and appear on the invoices), a Total of $4,99 due 24 Nov, the row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. Subscribe on Basic opened the same kind of screen for the plan Free: This app bills you for usage charges, You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it, the same spending limit of $99,00 USD per 30 days, Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. On neither screen was the sentence You will not be billed for this test charge shown, and both asked for a payment method, so nothing was approved.
